decisions.decision: sector_pack = commodities_energy (primary and only). bfsi_statements = false.
decisions.reason: NALCO is an integrated bauxite-alumina-aluminium producer with captive power (metals & mining). Both reportable segments (Chemicals=alumina, Aluminium) sit in the same value chain, so no secondary pack needed.

decisions.decision: R-SEGMENT fires literally (2 reportable segments), but both segments are one aluminium value chain. Plan: DR1 (company/management) may start in parallel with analysis; DR2 (sector/peers) waits until extraction confirms segment mix and external-vs-inter-segment alumina sales, then runs ONCE scoped to the aluminium value chain (LME aluminium price, alumina index, power/coal costs). Smaller targeted searches interleave between waves per user preference; research_loops_max=3.
decisions.reason: Segment count > 1 blocks R-PURE, but the segments share one industry — a per-segment DR2 branch would duplicate work. Extraction-first confirms mix cheaply; user explicitly prefers fluid, smaller in-between searches over monolithic research passes.

decisions.decision: Extract both bases. Preliminary primary basis = consolidated, to be confirmed at COMPUTE: NALCO's subsidiaries/JVs (Angul Aluminium Park, GACL-NALCO Alkalies JV, Utkarsha Aluminium Dhatu Nigam JV) are believed immaterial (<10% of revenue), in which case standalone becomes primary and consolidated the cross-check.
decisions.reason: Rule T4: consolidated primary only when subsidiaries material. Materiality not yet verifiable pre-extraction; decision flagged for confirmation and the standalone-vs-consolidated comparison table is mandatory either way.

decisions.decision: family = commodities_energy (unchanged); playbook = ferrous_non_ferrous_metals (newly assigned — the two-tier registry postdates this run).
decisions.reason: Re-run against state/business_model.json per prompts/02 T2-RECHECK. The value chain confirms a per-tonne spread business with captive bauxite; the 'Chemical' segment is metallurgical alumina, not specialty chemicals.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: shares the per-tonne spread structure and the `ebitda per tonne` keyword, but NALCO produces no clinker/cement and the market is global rather than freight-limited regional
the 1,200 MW CPP and 198.4 MW wind are captive inputs to smelting, not a merchant or regulated generation business; no PPA book and no regulated equity

the 'Chemical' reporting-segment NAME is misleading — the segment is metallurgical-grade alumina, a commodity intermediate priced off LME, not a specialty chemical. Classifying on the segment label rather than the economics would have routed this to the wrong playbook.

recheck.reason: T2-RECHECK run 2026-08-03 against state/business_model.json, which was written after the original triage. The value chain it maps (bauxite -> alumina -> aluminium, captive power, per_tonne unit economics) confirms the first pass. unit_denominator per_tonne matches the registry entry for this playbook.
